symptom:
A small TCP key-value server (server/main.go) appends every PUT as a checksummed key=value line to data/kv.log, fsyncs, and only then answers OK. On start it reads the log back, verifies each record and rebuilds its in-memory map. The client remembers every PUT that was answered OK and reads them all back at the end. The disk sometimes fails an fsync with EIO, in which case the server answers ERR to that PUT and keeps running; the unsynced writes stay readable in the page cache but are dropped from durable storage. A supervisor restarts the server when it exits.

Observed on seed 1: fsync failed with EIO at disk op #38 (287ms) and again at disk op #264 (2.8s), and the server was crashed at 852ms and during a disk operation at 1.95s. The client reported: acknowledged write lost: k0=v0, server now answers "NONE". The very first key was gone.

Expected: every PUT that returned OK must be readable after crashes and restarts, whatever happened to the PUTs that returned ERR.
